summary: Reworked the .NET and React paste workspace with explicit command contracts, capability headers, generated edit-key receipts, versioned updates/deletes and durable creation request receipts.

Replaced truncating aggregate writes with bounded validation, cooperating-process file leases, flushed same-directory replacement, readonly reads and explicit legacy migration with exact source backups.

Added retained and exportable drafts, explicit conflict review, exact creation retries after lost acknowledgements, public-only literal search and pagination, content copy and exact text downloads, forks and responsive forms.
Added nine detailed project-specific learning guides, historical markers on earlier documentation, pinned setup and meaningful client, backend, HTTP and browser verification.

checks.environment: Windows, .NET SDK 10.0.302 and net10.0, Node 22.16.0, React 19.2.6, Vite 8.0.14, Chromium 148 disposable profiles
checks.command: npm test; npm run build; dotnet build verification/BackendChecks/BackendChecks.csproj; dotnet verification/BackendChecks/bin/Debug/net10.0/BackendChecks.dll <fresh-output>; python verification/verify_http.py; python verification/verify_browser.py

limits: Loopback local learning application; no account/session system, public deployment or HTTPS termination. Unlisted pastes are directly link-readable. New random capabilities differ from migrated user-selected keys, whose original strength is retained.

Whole-workspace JSON persistence: maximum 20 MiB, 2000 stored pastes, 10000 creation receipts and 10000 activity entries. Expired records and creation history are not automatically purged or archived. Capacity rejects further changes.

File-lease coordination assumes cooperating processes on one local filesystem. Same-directory replacement and Windows sharing-failure tests do not establish all-filesystem atomicity, network-share support or arbitrary power-loss survival.

No key-rotation flow, account recovery, administrative audit UI, durable update/delete idempotency or automatic merge. Lost update acknowledgements require reviewing current data; creation retries use durable request receipts.

Migration supports the known legacy array only, preserves source bytes and refuses an existing workspace. Unsupported or inconsistent records require review in a copy; historical view metadata is preserved but new reads do not count views. Legacy key entry supports 6 through 256 characters; longer historical keys require review using the preserved earlier application/data, because a hash alone cannot reveal the original key length.

Draft and receipt exports are local manual-recovery artifacts. Browser evidence does not establish full accessibility conformance, all-browser compatibility, production scalability or operational backup certification. System clipboard line endings can follow the platform; raw responses and text downloads retain exact stored bytes.
